claims.statement: The revised EU Energy Performance of Buildings Directive strengthens EPCs, introduces building renovation passports, and gradually sets minimum energy-performance standards for non-residential stock.
A renovation passport is described as a tailored staged roadmap prepared with an expert, which supports an expert-tool distribution model rather than a direct-to-owner calculator.

Hypothesis: assessors, property managers, and lenders will pay for a shared calculation and evidence schema because portfolios need comparable staged plans, while each country's implementation creates local workflow complexity.

contrary_evidence: The EU describes renovation passports as voluntary, so demand depends on national implementation, financing, and expert workflow value rather than a universal immediate mandate.
EPC and building-energy software incumbents can add staged-planning modules.

economics.acquisition_route: Start with a Polish assessor software or property manager, then distribute through lender and building-software integrations
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 20000 annual small-building passports plus 15 enterprise licences could reach 5-7 million PLN ARR in years 6-8; at 25% EBITDA, 6x EBITDA, and 75% founder ownership, founder equity could exceed 5.6 million PLN
economics.founder_time: 16-22 hours weekly for one-country MVP, declining to 8-12 hours weekly after expert partners own surveys and partner support
economics.gross_margin_basis: Scenario calculation and document generation can support 80-90% gross margin; local benchmark maintenance and enterprise integrations are the main costs
economics.payback: Target under 9 months for an assessor platform and under 15 months for a lender integration; partners must save report labour or increase financed project conversion
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 150-500 PLN per residential passport, 1000-5000 PLN per commercial building, and 50000-250000 PLN annual platform licences
economics.retention_or_repeat: Passports are versioned as measures are completed, portfolios are monitored annually, and financing scenarios update with prices and performance

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Local measure-cost benchmarks, realised energy outcomes, building archetypes, and lender-accepted evidence templates improve recommendations
fingerprint.customer: Energy-performance assessors, commercial property managers, banks, green-lending platforms, and building-software vendors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded in EPC assessor tools, property-management systems, bank technical due diligence, and green-loan workflows
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Calculation, scenario, evidence, and portfolio API with per-building and enterprise licensing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Assessor, property manager, or lender pays per issued passport or per building under annual portfolio monitoring
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An EPC, portfolio review, refinancing, sale, or renovation decision requires a staged and comparable investment roadmap

founder_fit: Strong renewable-energy, modelling, finance, and family-business adjacency, with an assessor and lender channel that avoids homeowner-by-homeowner selling. The family company could validate workflow assumptions on non-confidential cases, while accredited experts own certification.
risks: Poor recommendations can misallocate large renovation budgets; professionals must own final reports.
Country-specific calculation rules can turn expansion into consulting-heavy maintenance.
Property-data integrations and lender security reviews may extend sales cycles.

structure.control_point: The signed staged-renovation plan used to prioritise works and support financing or portfolio decisions
structure.critical_dependency: Accredited partner adoption and locally valid calculation and cost data accepted by owners and lenders

thesis: Provide energy-performance assessors, property managers, and green-lending platforms with an API that converts an EPC and building survey into a staged renovation passport: measures, dependencies, cost ranges, energy and carbon scenarios, financing evidence, and versioned assumptions. The accredited professional signs the result; the software becomes the reusable calculation and portfolio-data layer.
title: Renovation Passport Engine
uncertainties: Polish transposition details, assessor accreditation, and approved calculation methods need confirmation.
Banks may accept only their own technical due-diligence formats.
Cost and performance estimates require local calibration and may become stale quickly.
